page: UpCloud HICPU-64xCPU-96GB is a compute-focused virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 physical cores of the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The system is configured with a shared CPU allocation model. It includes 96.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.5 GB of RAM per core, alongside a bundled 200 GB local SSD and one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results indicate a strong multi-threaded performance profile, particularly in parallelized workloads. The server achieves strong results in bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 397.84 GB/sec, PassMark CPU score at 61581.11, and PassMark CPU physics testing at 7970.6. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the bottom 10% at 785.2 and Geekbench single-core scoring at an average 1316.0. Memory bandwidth is average, with uncached read speeds of 113.09 GB/sec and write speeds of 63.93 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and high core count, this server offers a high density of virtual resources, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for highly parallelized, non-latency-sensitive tasks. It is well-suited for multi-threaded decompression, ray tracing, and batch processing workloads. However, the shared CPU model and weak single-core performance make it less ideal for single-threaded applications, large-scale database operations, or large-model LLM inference, where prompt processing for 70B models drops to a weak 6.76 tokens/sec.
